newsitem.title: USA: Iraq to deliver aid annexes on Mon - Iraq official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to deliver aid annexes on Mon - Iraq official.

text.p: Iraq will deliver annexes to its aid distribution plan to the United Nations on Monday, allowing the U.N. to review and accept the document in the next few days, according to a spokesman for the Iraqi mission to the United Nations in New York.
The annexes arrived from Baghdad as expected over the weekend and "they will be delivered today," the official said.
Iraq has stalled in delivering its aid plan for nearly two months, delaying the restart of oil exports under the second round of the "oil-for-food" scheme with Iraq.
Under the terms of the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell up to $2 billion of oil over 180 days in two equal 90-day instalments.

U.N. officials said on Monday that they expect to approve the deal this week. But the delay in restarting the second round means Iraq will either have to sell oil at a rate of between 1.5 and two million barrels per day during August and the first week in September or forego some of its quarterly allotment, Western diplomats said.
